title: Detector artefacts: could partial charge loss turn a 71 keV electron recoil into the LZ event?
question: Which instrumental mechanisms (electron lifetime, local absorber/impurity plume, field or extraction defect, S2 clipping/truncation, S1-S2 mis-pairing) could remove 78% of a ~70 keV ER's ionisation electrons while preserving S1, pulse shape and position; what magnitude and signature does each require; which do LZ's stated checks exclude; and what residual probability remains?
headline_result: A 69.6 keV ER needs 78% post-recombination charge loss (f = 269/1226 = 0.219), 3-25x any published detector scale; a bulk lifetime excursion to 566 us would be witnessed by ~84/h long-drift beta/alpha events (P(silent 300 s) = 9e-4); a localised absorber probable enough (area fraction 1e-3) predicts 65-101 charge-deficient ERs in the empty band below the ER cloud (Fig. 4: zero points at S1c 520-800, log S2c 4.15-4.30) and a 19-61 sigma hole in the 83mKr S2c map; clipping/truncation excluded by the alpha-template shape (75-149x larger pulses; remnant sigma 0.48); artefact residual ~0.006 vs dossier prior 0.18
key_numbers: f_req 0.219 (nestpy 0.201); ER mean logS2c 4.626, grey edge 4.37, strip 4.15-4.30 empty at S1c 520-800; tau_e 566/536/508 us for tau_cal inf/10/5 ms; uncorrected 2.5/5/10 ms loses 29/16/8%; NR window drift 715-878 us (18% FV); science 0.32/h (0.067 at t>800); monitors 155/h (112-239), 84/h at t>500; P(silent) 0.79/0.50/0.25/9e-4/8e-7/3e-37 for 10/30/60/300/600/3600 s; tau window 554-680 us (0.045); sigma_T 3.07 mm, sigma_t 1.49 us; footprint 1.19 cm2 of 16650; disk p_V 0.012-0.023, p_V/(p_V+p_E) 0.10-0.16; N_par 5261 (x0.5-2); eps for N_V=0.1: 0.8-1.6e-3 -> 65-101 affected ERs; ML P(obs) 0.038-0.059; Kr 6-60/cm2 -> 19-61 sigma; plume tau_loc 1.4-14 us (x350-3500); extraction 0.175, deficit x4.56 = 18x map; truncation sigma 0.48 skew -1.25; alpha S2 75-149x event; residual 0.006 (x32)
model_or_mechanism: post-recombination charge-loss mechanisms in a dual-phase TPC: exponential lifetime loss vs drift, Gaussian electron cloud (diffusion) meeting an absorbing disk (Marcum-Q loss distribution), extraction-efficiency dip, truncated/clipped S2; population budget against the Fig. 4 grey ER population and the 83mKr S2c map; judgement-based channel prior x survival factors
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - disfavours the detector-artefact class; does not discriminate DM from other origins
confidence: medium - mechanism sizes and the empty-strip population argument are robust; channel priors, survival factors and several detector scales (diffusion, lifetime, Rn, 83mKr statistics, extraction efficiency) are judgement or recalled
